introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0560 History 1, June 2026, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). One and a half hours. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is correct and mark only one answer for each question (if you mark more than one answer you score zero for that question). Use a soft HB pencil, avoid spending too much time on any one question, and do all rough work in the booklet. Mobile phones are not allowed in the examination room.

questions.enonce_markdown:
In which of the following battles in the Cameroon campaign of 1914-1916 did the Allies suffer considerable human and material losses?

*Options as printed:* A) Garoua   B) Nsanakang   C) Douala   D) Mora
questions.corrige_markdown:
At the start of the campaign the Allies suffered setbacks in the north and west. A British force attacking the German position at Garoua in August 1914 was repulsed, and at Nsanakang in September 1914 German troops defeated British forces: the Allies lost men and equipment there. By contrast, Douala fell without a real battle on 27 September 1914, when the Germans chose not to defend the coast against the Anglo-French force, and Mora, the last German post, was besieged until February 1916 and then surrendered. The usual textbook answer is Nsanakang, but Garoua is also a defensible answer, so the question is not reliable enough to be auto-marked.

**Intended answer: B (Nsanakang).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
One of the following decisions was not taken in the Mamfe Conference of 1953.

*Options as printed:* A) Decided to cut off political connections with Nigeria   B) Transformed the Benevolent Neutrality Bloc into a political party   C) Requested for the formation of the KNDP   D) Demanded a separate Regional status
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Mamfe Conference of 1953 was a meeting of Southern Cameroons leaders after the Eastern Regional crisis. Its main demands were that the Southern Cameroons should break its political link with the Eastern Region of Nigeria and be given a separate regional status (options A and D, understood in that sense). The KNDP (Kamerun National Democratic Party) was only founded later, in 1955, after John Ngu Foncha broke with Dr E.M.L. Endeley's KNC, so a request for its formation cannot have been made at Mamfe in 1953. Option B also refers to the origins of the KNDP, whose exact timing is not firmly established, so the printed question has two possible answers (B and C). The answer expected is C, but the question is left open for self-assessment.

**Intended answer: C (Requested for the formation of the KNDP).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the political party that was forcefully launched in 1990 in the context of the re-introduction of multi-party politics in Cameroon...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Social Democratic Front (SDF) was launched in Bamenda on 26 May 1990 by John Fru Ndi and others, in defiance of a government ban on new parties, and several people were killed when the security forces intervened. It was the first major opposition party of the return to multi-party politics. The CDU (Cameroon Democratic Union) was founded by Adamou Ndam Njoya in 1991, the UNDP (National Union for Democracy and Progress) was another party of the early 1990s, and the UPC dates from 1948, so none of them is the party launched by force in May 1990. **Answer: D.**
themes: return to multi-party politics in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: The concept in which the solidarity and the unity of the African continent is promoted is called...
questions.corrige_markdown: Pan-Africanism is the idea and movement that Africans and people of African descent share common interests and should unite to defend them. Neo-colonialism, imperialism and colonialism all describe forms of foreign domination, the opposite of African unity. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the national forum that sat in 2019 to address petitions on crisis in the North West and South West Regions of Cameroon.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Major National Dialogue was convened by President Paul Biya and held in Yaounde from 30 September to 4 October 2019 to discuss the crisis in the North West and South West Regions, among other national questions. The National Commission for the Promotion of Bilingualism and Multiculturalism was created in 2017 as a permanent body, not as a forum that sat in 2019. The other two names do not correspond to the forum of 2019. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The National Commission for Bilingualism and Multi-Culturalism

questions.enonce_markdown: The Cameroon coastal settlement headed by Lock Priso that refused to recognise the Germano - Duala treaty of 1884 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Lock Priso (Bele Bele) was the chief of Hickory Town (Bonaberi), on the opposite bank of the Wouri from Bell and Akwa towns. He refused to accept the treaty that Kings Bell and Akwa signed with the Germans in July 1884. In December 1884 a German naval force attacked and destroyed Hickory Town to impose German authority. Bell Town and Akwa Town were the two signatory towns. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The formation of the UNO in 1945 was concluded at...
questions.corrige_markdown: The United Nations Charter was drawn up and signed at the San Francisco Conference (April to June 1945; signed on 26 June 1945). Teheran (1943), Yalta (February 1945) and Potsdam (July 1945) were meetings of the Allied leaders on the war and the post-war settlement, where the idea of the UNO was discussed but its formation was not concluded. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The immediate result of the 1953 Eastern Regional crisis in Southern Cameroons was...
questions.corrige_markdown: In 1953 the Southern Cameroons members of the Eastern House of Assembly at Enugu walked out after a dispute over leadership of the Eastern Region, and the crisis led Southern Cameroons to demand separation from the East. The result was the Lyttelton Constitution of 1954, which gave the Southern Cameroons a quasi-regional status with its own House of Assembly and Executive Council. The two provinces (Cameroons and Bamenda) dated from the 1920s and the KNC (Kamerun National Congress) was formed in 1951, so neither was a result of the crisis; a House of Chiefs was set up later, around 1960. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The creation of the House of Assembly
The Creation of the House of Chiefs

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the French High Commissioner often associated with the ban on the UPC in French Cameroon during the 1950s.
questions.corrige_markdown: Roland Pre was French High Commissioner in Cameroon from 1954 to 1956. The UPC was banned by a decree of 13 July 1955, after the riots of May 1955, while he was in office. Andre Soucadaux (High Commissioner 1949-1954) and Pierre Messmer (1956-1958) held office before and after him, and the UPC was already under heavy pressure before 1955. **Answer: D.**
themes: upc and french repression in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the Treaty of the Paris Peace Settlement of 1919-1920 signed with the major Central Powers which was most criticized.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Treaty of Versailles (28 June 1919) was signed with Germany, the leading Central Power. It was the most criticised because Germany was forced to accept the war guilt clause, pay reparations, give up territory and its colonies and limit its army; Germans called it a diktat. St Germain (Austria) and Trianon (Hungary) were also signed with Central Powers but were less known, and Lausanne (1923) replaced the Treaty of Sevres with Turkey and is not part of the 1919-1920 series. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The African country in which a civil war broke out immediately after independence was?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Belgian Congo became independent on 30 June 1960, and within days it fell into the Congo crisis: an army mutiny, the secession of Katanga and then a civil conflict with foreign intervention and a UN force. Gabon (independent in 1960) did not experience a civil war after independence; the civil war in Chad began in 1965 and the Nigerian civil war (Biafra) in 1967, several years after independence. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A political effect of the Second World War on Africa and international relations was...

*Options as printed:* A) The weakening of the grip of colonial powers over their colonies   B) The formation of the West African Student Union (WASU)   C) shattering the myth of European invincibility   D) The creation of the UNO
questions.corrige_markdown:
The war exhausted Britain and France, which could no longer control their empires as before, and it encouraged the nationalist movements: the weakening of the grip of the colonial powers over their colonies was a major political effect. The West African Student Union was founded in London in 1925, long before the war, so option B is wrong. Options C and D can also be argued: the defeat of France in 1940 and the Japanese victories damaged the myth of European invincibility, and the creation of the UNO (1945) changed international relations. The expected answer is A, but the question has more than one defensible answer and is left open for self-assessment.

**Intended answer: A (The weakening of the grip of colonial powers over their colonies).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.
themes: impact of world war two on africa

questions.enonce_markdown: An important condition for European powers to claim colonies in Africa at the Berlin West Africa Conference was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Berlin West Africa Conference (1884-1885) laid down the principle of effective occupation: a European power could claim a coastal territory only if it really occupied it, with an administration and some force, and notified the other powers. Treaties with African rulers were used as evidence but were not the rule laid down; middleman monopoly was the position of the coastal African traders, not a condition for the Europeans. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The political leader in Southern Cameroons who became Leader of Government Business in 1954 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Dr Emmanuel Mbella Lifafa Endeley, leader of the KNC, became Leader of Government Business in the Southern Cameroons when the Lyttelton Constitution of 1954 gave the territory quasi-regional status; he became Premier in 1958. John Foncha, leader of the KNDP, only came to power in the elections of January 1959. S.T. Muna and S.A. George were other Southern Cameroons politicians who did not hold this post. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following countries involved in the scramble for Africa acquired the Congo as a result of the Berlin Act of 1885?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Berlin Act of 1885 recognised the Congo basin as the Congo Free State, the personal possession of King Leopold II of the Belgians; Belgium itself took it over as the Belgian Congo in 1908. Of the four countries, Belgium is the one that acquired the Congo. France had the French Congo north of the river, Portugal kept Angola and Germany had no part of the Congo. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The most significant reason for Cameroon becoming a mandated territory in 1922 was because...

*Options as printed:* A) German rule in Cameroon had ended   B) The League of Nations' decision   C) Germany lost Cameroon as a colony   D) Britain and France defeated the Germans in the territory in 1916
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon became a mandate because Germany was defeated in the First World War and, under the Treaty of Versailles (1919), gave up all its colonies; the victors did not annex them but placed them under the League of Nations mandate system, which was confirmed for Cameroon in 1922. The most significant reason is therefore that Germany lost the colony. The decision of the League of Nations (B) is the formal act and is also defensible, while A and D describe the situation before 1919 (the Allied conquest of 1914-1916). The question has two defensible answers and is left open for self-assessment.

**Intended answer: C (Germany lost Cameroon as a colony).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the public secondary school opened by President Ahidjo in 1961 in West Cameroon to promote bilingualism.
questions.corrige_markdown: The question asks for a bilingual school in West Cameroon, the former Southern Cameroons. Options A and D are in Yaounde and Douala, which are in East Cameroon, and B is a Government Grammar School with no bilingual status in its name. The Government Bilingual Grammar School at Man-O-War Bay, near Victoria (Limbe), is the school created in the early 1960s as part of the policy of promoting bilingualism between the two parts of the Federation. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Government Bilingual Grammar School, Man-O-War Bay

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following groups of towns in Cameroon served as seats of the German Colonial Administration in the years 1885, 1902, and 1909?
questions.corrige_markdown: The German administration began at Douala (Kamerun town), where the first Governor, Julius von Soden, was based from 1885. The capital was moved to Buea, on the slopes of Mount Cameroon, around 1901 and 1902 under Governor Jesko von Puttkamer, and Yaounde, a German station in the interior since 1889, appears as the third seat of administration in the question (1909). Only option A follows this order of Douala, Buea and Yaounde. The exact dates of the changes are not firmly established. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A political method adopted by the Germans to consolidate their position in Cameroon between 1884-1916 was the...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Germans consolidated their position by force: they created a colonial army, the Schutztruppe (with police units), which conquered the interior and put down resistance. This is a political and military method. Commercial plantations (B) and roads and railways (C) were economic measures, and the Master Race Theory (A) was a later Nazi ideology, not a method of German rule in Cameroon before 1916. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Great Britain's reason for declaring war on Germany in 1914 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Britain had guaranteed Belgian neutrality by the Treaty of London (1839). When Germany invaded Belgium on 4 August 1914 as part of the Schlieffen Plan, Britain declared war the same day. The assassination of the Archduke and the Austrian declaration on Serbia were earlier events that started the crisis, and the USA only entered the war in 1917. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Serbian assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
Austrian declaration of war on Serbia

questions.enonce_markdown: Paul Biya became President of Cameroon in 1982 because he...
questions.corrige_markdown: President Ahmadou Ahidjo resigned on 4 November 1982. Paul Biya, who was Prime Minister since 1975, succeeded him because the constitution (as amended in 1975) provided that the Prime Minister takes over when the President resigns or is unable to serve: he was the constitutional successor. Education, popularity and his earlier post at the Presidency are not the legal reason. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Was once Secretary General at the Presidency

questions.enonce_markdown: The first Speaker of the National Assembly after the introduction of the Unitary State was?
questions.corrige_markdown: After the referendum of 20 May 1972 the Federation became the United Republic of Cameroon, and the single National Assembly that replaced the federal and state assemblies was presided over by Solomon Tandeng Muna, a former Prime Minister of West Cameroon, from 1973 to 1988. Foncha had been Vice-President of the Federation until 1970, Fonka Shang Lawrence became Speaker later, and P.M. Kale had been Prime Minister of West Cameroon. The dates are given from memory and should be checked in a textbook. **Answer: B.**
themes: creation of the united republic of cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: The Assembly in French Cameroon which came into being as a result of the Loi Cadre reforms of 1956 but with limited powers of legislation was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Loi Cadre (Defferre law) of 1956 gave the overseas territories a measure of self-government. In Cameroon it turned the Territorial Assembly (ATCAM) into the Legislative Assembly of Cameroon (ALCAM), elected in December 1956, with limited powers of legislation. ARCAM (1946) and ATCAM (1952) were earlier assemblies, and RACAM does not exist. **Answer: C.**
themes: loi cadre reforms in french cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: Territories under the mandate system were classified according to the level of development. In which category was Cameroon placed?
questions.corrige_markdown: The League of Nations divided the mandates into A, B and C. Category A (former Turkish territories of the Middle East) were thought nearly ready for independence; Category B (Cameroon, Togoland and Tanganyika in tropical Africa) were less developed and were to be administered under conditions such as the ban on the arms trade; Category C (South West Africa and the Pacific islands) were treated almost as part of the mandatory power. There was no Category D. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The U. N. specialized agency charged with the alleviation of poverty, hunger and the promotion of rural development is...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) works against hunger and poverty and for agriculture and rural development. WHO deals with health, the IMF with monetary co-operation and financial stability, and UNICEF with the rights and welfare of children. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which one of the following European countries was attacked by Germany in 1939 leading to the outbreak of the Second World War?
questions.corrige_markdown: Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, and Britain and France declared war on Germany two days later. Austria (1938) and Czechoslovakia (1938-1939) had been taken without war, and Albania was invaded by Italy in April 1939. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which year was the U.N. Charter signed in a conference in the USA?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Charter was signed by fifty countries at the San Francisco Conference on 26 June 1945 and came into force on 24 October 1945. 1943 and 1944 were years of preparation (Moscow, Dumbarton Oaks) and 1946 was the year of the first General Assembly. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which missionary body was the first to establish mission stations in Cameroon in the 1850s?
questions.corrige_markdown: The English Baptist Missionary Society was the first to work in Cameroon: Joseph Merrick and Alfred Saker started in the 1840s and Saker founded the mission at Douala in 1845 and the settlement of Victoria in 1858. The Basel Mission and the American Presbyterians arrived in the 1870s and 1880s and the Catholic Pallottines in 1890. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The colonial policy by which Africans were treated like a father treating his children was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Paternalism is the attitude by which the colonial power acted as a father who knows best for Africans, who were treated as children needing guidance. Indirect rule governed through African chiefs, assimilation tried to turn Africans into French citizens, and association respected local institutions in a limited way. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The incident leading to the Japanese invasion of China in 1931 took place in the town of...
questions.corrige_markdown: On 18 September 1931 an explosion on the South Manchurian Railway near Mukden was used by the Japanese army as a pretext to occupy Manchuria. Manchuria is the region, not a town, and Jehol was invaded in 1933. The League of Nations failed to stop Japan, which weakened collective security. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The German statesman in the 1930s whose objective was to resist the Versailles treaty and rearm Germany was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Adolf Hitler, Chancellor from January 1933, set out to destroy the Treaty of Versailles: he left the League of Nations in 1933, reintroduced conscription and built the air force in 1935 and reoccupied the Rhineland in 1936. Bismarck ruled in the nineteenth century, Hindenburg was the ageing President and Goering was one of Hitler's lieutenants. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Mandate System of the League of Nations was introduced in Cameroon in...
questions.corrige_markdown: The mandate over Cameroon was conferred on Britain and France by the League of Nations in 1922 (Council decision of 20 July 1922). 1916 was the year of the Anglo-French partition of the territory, 1919 the year of the Treaty of Versailles and the Covenant of the League, and 1920 the year the League began working. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main aim of the Mau-Mau movement in the decolonisation process in Kenya in the 1950s was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Mau Mau, mostly Kikuyu, began an armed revolt in 1952 against British rule and white settlers who had taken their land; their aim was land and freedom, that is, to fight for independence. Positive Action and non-violence was Kwame Nkrumah's policy in the Gold Coast. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Equality in education and employment opportunities

questions.enonce_markdown: In an interview with Cameroon Tribune in February 1983, President Ahidjo revealed that he resigned as Head of State because...
questions.corrige_markdown: Ahidjo announced his resignation on 4 November 1982 and explained it by his state of health and fatigue. He had been re-elected in 1980 for a term that had not ended, and he presented the decision as a personal one, not as a loss of popularity. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: He was feeling tired due to poor health
He had completed his Presidential Mandate
He had been too long in power

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following revolts against the French during the Mandate period was the most violent, leading to the death of its leader?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Baya (Gbaya) revolt, the Kongo-Wara war of 1928-1931 in the east of French Cameroon, was led by the prophet Karnou (Barka Ngainoumbey), who was killed in December 1928; the fighting went on until about 1931 and was put down violently by the French. The Duala resistance to the Germans (Rudolf Duala Manga Bell) belongs to the German period, and the Fulbe and the Bamum did not stage a comparable revolt against the French. **Answer: D.**
themes: revolts in french cameroon under the mandate

questions.enonce_markdown: The prominent German merchant who influenced the German government to annex Cameroon in 1884 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Adolf Woermann, the Hamburg shipowner and trader with the largest firm on the Cameroon coast, put pressure on Chancellor Bismarck to protect German trade there; his agents, Edward Schmidt and Johannes Voss, took part in the treaty of July 1884. Hewett was the British Consul who arrived too late to sign treaties. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The first Cameroon pressure group created to express the political aspirations of Cameroonians and support French hold in the territory was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Jeunesse Camerounaise Francaise (JEUCAFRA), set up in Douala in the late 1930s by young educated Cameroonians, was a pressure group which accepted French rule and asked for reforms and more participation. The Union Camerounaise (Ahidjo, 1958) and the UPC (1948) were political parties founded later, and the USCC was a trade union confederation. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Union des Syndicats Confederes du Cameroun (USCC)

questions.enonce_markdown:
The British Resident who introduced the payment of fees in hospitals in order to subsidise the cost of medical care to natives was...

*Options as printed:* A) Elphinston   B) Arnet   C) Rutherford   D) Aveling
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Resident often linked in textbooks and in other GCE questions with hospital fees in the Cameroons Province is E.J. Arnett, who served in the second half of the 1920s and the early 1930s. This link could not be verified from an independent source, and the other three names could not be excluded, so the question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically. The answer expected is B (Arnett), to be checked in the history textbook.

**Intended answer: B (Arnet).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Appeasement encouraged German aggression in the 1930s by all of the following except...

*Options as printed:* A) Encouraging Germany to reclaim her colonies in Africa   B) Justifying Hitler's claims to territorial demands   C) Making the great powers sympathetic with Germany's demands   D) Making friendship with Hitler
questions.corrige_markdown:
Appeasement meant giving way to Hitler's demands (the Rhineland, the Anschluss, the Sudetenland at Munich in 1938) to avoid war. It encouraged him because it made his claims look just (B), made the other powers sympathetic to some of his demands (C) and showed that Britain and France were friendly and unwilling to resist (D). The powers never actively encouraged Germany to reclaim colonies in Africa, so option A is the one that does not fit. The wording is loose, however: colonial concessions were sometimes discussed by Britain, and 'making friendship with Hitler' is not a precise effect, so the question is left open for self-assessment.

**Intended answer: A (Encouraging Germany to reclaim her colonies in Africa).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Select the Southern Cameroons Prime Minister who led the delegation to the Foumban Conference in July 1961.
questions.corrige_markdown: John Ngu Foncha, leader of the KNDP and Prime Minister of the Southern Cameroons since 1959, led the Southern Cameroons delegation at the Foumban Constitutional Conference (17-21 July 1961), where the future Federal constitution was discussed with the government of Ahmadou Ahidjo. Endeley was the leader of the opposition, while Jua and Muna were members of Foncha's team. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following towns was proposed as the Federal capital by the Southern Cameroons delegation at the Foumban Conference but was rejected?

*Options as printed:* A) Buea   B) Bamenda   C) Yaounde   D) Douala
questions.corrige_markdown:
The Foumban Constitutional Conference (17-21 July 1961) discussed the form of the Federation between the Republic of Cameroon and the Southern Cameroons. The Southern Cameroons delegation, led by John Foncha, made proposals about the structure of the Federation, and Ahmadou Ahidjo's side kept Yaounde as the Federal capital. Which town the Southern Cameroons delegation proposed instead could not be established with certainty from the sources that could be checked, and none of the options can be confirmed. The question is therefore left open for self-assessment and should be checked in the history textbook used in class (Foumban Conference).

**Intended answer: not established.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following was a political reason for nationalist activities in the Gold Coast from 1945-1957?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Burns Constitution of 1946 gave Africans only a minority of seats in the Legislative Council and left real power with the Governor, so nationalists demanded self-government: this is a political cause. The rise in prices was an economic cause (with the 1948 riots), and the presence of many educated people was a social factor; the improvement of transport was not a cause of nationalism. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The weaknesses of the Burns constitution
The rapid rise in prices of consumer goods
The presence of many educated elites

questions.enonce_markdown: The city hosting the Headquarters of the UNO is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The headquarters of the United Nations are in New York, on land along the East River. Geneva was the seat of the League of Nations (and hosts a UN office), The Hague is the seat of the International Court of Justice, and London was the seat of the first General Assembly in 1946. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which of the following French African colonies was the policy of Assimilation most effective?
questions.corrige_markdown: Assimilation worked best in Senegal, where the inhabitants of the four communes (Dakar, Saint-Louis, Goree and Rufisque) were French citizens, voted and sent a deputy to Paris. In Mali, Ivory Coast and Chad most people remained subjects. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following options did the United Nations Organization leave out from the February 1961 plebiscite in British Cameroons?
questions.corrige_markdown: The plebiscite of 11 February 1961 offered the Southern Cameroons only two choices: to join the independent Federation of Nigeria or to join the independent Republic of Cameroon. The UN did not allow the third choice, separate independence for the Southern Cameroons, which some Southern Cameroons leaders had asked for. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Reunification with the Republic of Cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: The French colonial policy which gave the French colonial administrators the powers to inflict disciplinary penalties on natives without trial was called?
questions.corrige_markdown: The indigenat (native code) allowed French administrators to punish Africans (the subjects, not the citizens) with fines or short imprisonment without going to court. Assimilation and association were general policies, and prestation was the forced labour obligation (days of unpaid work on roads and public works). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A socio-economic effect of the First World War on Cameroon was the...
questions.corrige_markdown: The war cost many lives (soldiers, carriers and civilians) and it disrupted the German plantations, whose owners were expelled or whose production stopped, so it had social and economic effects. The partition of Cameroon between Britain and France and the loss of Cameroon territory by Germany were political effects. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Unrest, insecurity and disorder in some parts of the territory
Loss of lives and disruption of German plantations

questions.enonce_markdown: A former German territory that was partitioned and became a mandated territory of the League of Nations was...
questions.corrige_markdown: Togoland, like Cameroon, was divided between Britain and France in 1916 and placed under a mandate of the League of Nations in 1922. Zanzibar was never German. South West Africa went whole to South Africa. Tanganyika also lost small parts (Ruanda-Urundi to Belgium), so the question is not perfectly worded, but Togoland is the standard example of a partitioned German colony. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: At independence, the Republic of Cameroon and the British Southern Cameroons merged into a...
questions.corrige_markdown: On 1 October 1961 the Southern Cameroons joined the Republic of Cameroon to form the Federal Republic of Cameroon, made of two federated states (East and West Cameroon). The unitary state came only in 1972, and the 'decentralized unitary state' is the form in the 1996 constitution. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An economic motive for the German success in signing the annexation treaty with the Douala Chiefs in 1884 was...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Duala chiefs, Bell and Akwa, lived by acting as middlemen between the European traders on the coast and the peoples of the interior. The treaty of 12 July 1884 secured their trade rights and monopoly, and this economic guarantee was an important reason for their agreement. Gifts or bribes (A) and the gunboat (C) were other pressures, but they are not the economic motive; the friendly attitude of the traders (B) is not an economic motive either. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Due to bribes given to the Douala Chiefs
The friendly attitude of the German traders
The frightful presence of the German gunboat
The promise to respect native trade monopoly
